earlier_scan.note: Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive descriptions are a wordlist or less only (Z'graggen 1975/1980, Claassen & McElhanon 1970); no grammar/phonology exists

sources.citation: Priestley, Carol. 2008. A grammar of Koromu (Kesawai): a Trans New Guinea language of Papua New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University (hdl 1885/150382).
sources.note: Describes the SISTER language Kesawai/Koromu [xes], not Sausi: sec. 2.3.2 p.40 'The main stress is on the penultimate syllable.. Alternating stress occurs on every other even-numbered syllable'. On Sausi it only says (p.8 fn.5) that Sausi was called Witi at the SIL Alphabet Development Workshop in 2000, that speakers gave her the name Wiya with a wordlist she collected in 1979, and that Sausi is the language most similar to Koromu.

sources.citation: O'Bannon, Devin, Mary O'Bannon, North Cady & April Hope. 2022. Kou Survey Report: A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Kou/Sensauru [snz] Language of Madang Province. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-017. Dallas: SIL International. 59 pp.

sources.citation: Carrington, Lois. 1996. A linguistic bibliography of the New Guinea area. Pacific Linguistics D-90. Canberra: Australian National University. xxvi+771 pp.
sources.note: no phonology content (bibliography); establishes absence of any pre-1996 Sausi description

sources.citation: Z'graggen, Johannes A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Rai Coast languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-30. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. Sausi is language B3; introduction sec. 7 says transcription is 'semiphonemic' and lists only segmental fluctuations for Sausi (glottal stop ~ g/k; ~ r); wordlist forms carry length marks but no stress marks (checked page scan).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, Johannes A. 1975. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1, 569-612. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.note: Nothing; classification of the Evapia family (Sinsauru, Asas, Sausi, Kesawai, Dumpu) and comparative vocabulary only.
sources.venue: New Guinea area languages and language study

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1975. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: Australian National University. vi+154 pp. + map.
sources.note: No phonology content. The volume is a classification with lexicostatistical remarks and village/population lists; for Sausi it gives the village list and (pp.13-14) 'B1 Sinsauru-B2 Asas and B3 Sausi-B4 Kesawai are dialects sharing more than 81% vocabulary'. The words stress/accent/tone do not occur.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, Johannes A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19.
sources.note: Does not cover Sausi (Rai Coast western section surveyed only 1971-73); no stress discussion found.

sources.citation: Claassen, Oren R. & Kenneth A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Finisterre Range - New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 11, 45-78. Pacific Linguistics A-23.
sources.note: Sec. 6.1.3 gives one paragraph of segmental notes for the Evapia family (stops, nasals, vibrant, lateral, five vowels); nothing on stress. Their 'Koropa' wordlist is Asas, not Sausi, per Z'graggen 1975.
Nothing; confirms current name Wia, endangered.
